en.title: News and television
en.summary: Headlines, news reports and talking about programmes.

paragraphs: News is written and spoken in a particular style, with short headlines and past tenses. This lesson shows you how to read and report the news in everyday conversation.
A family in Glasgow is watching the evening news together.

lines.speaker: Dad
lines.text: Turn up the volume, please. The weather is on.

lines.speaker: Mum
lines.text: The headlines said there was a storm in the north.

lines.speaker: Dad
lines.text: It's going to reach us tomorrow. They say the winds could be very strong.

lines.speaker: Son
lines.text: Does that mean school will be closed?

lines.speaker: Mum
lines.text: I don't think so, but the head teacher said that she would send a message if it was.

lines.speaker: Son
lines.text: Can we watch a film afterwards?

lines.speaker: Dad
lines.text: After the news. I want to hear the sports results.

lines.speaker: Mum
lines.text: I'd rather watch the quiz show.

paragraphs: **1. News is reported in the past tense.** Even when the news is recent, the main verbs are in the past simple or the present perfect for a recent event. See Introduction to Grammar: Past tenses.

blocks.html:
HeadlineFull sentence
Storm hits northA storm has hit the north.
PM resignsThe Prime Minister has resigned.
Floods close roadsFloods have closed several roads.
Team wins cupThe team won the cup.

paragraphs: **2. Reported speech tells what others said.** The tense shifts back one step, and said or told introduces the report. See Introduction to Grammar: Reported speech.

blocks.html:
DirectReported
"I will send a message."She said that she would send a message.
"The wind is strong."They said the wind was strong.
"We have closed the road."They said they had closed the road.
"Stay indoors."They told people to stay indoors.

items: A headline is the title of a news story, and a forecast is a prediction of the weather.
Channel means a television station, and a programme is a single broadcast.
Would rather means prefer: I'd rather watch the quiz show.
Breaking news is a story that has just happened.

paragraphs: The BBC is the national public broadcaster of the United Kingdom, paid for by a licence fee rather than advertising. Many people now watch news on their phones as well as on television.
